summary_en: This study tests whether optimizing ancillary therapies can improve the effect of immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment in people with solid tumors. The optimized regimen includes aspirin and loratadine, plus avoiding acetaminophen and THC-containing products, and participants receive it alongside standard immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. The main outcome is not stated; the stated goal is to compare efficacy with a matched historical control group, and the study is Phase 2.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si optimizar las terapias auxiliares puede mejorar el efecto del tratamiento con inhibidores de puntos de control inmunitario en personas con tumores sólidos. El esquema optimizado incluye aspirina y loratadina, además de evitar el acetaminofén y los productos que contienen THC, y los participantes lo reciben junto con el tratamiento estándar con inhibidores de puntos de control inmunitario. El resultado principal no se indica; el objetivo declarado es comparar la eficacia con un grupo de control histórico pareado, y el estudio es de Fase 2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 99 years with solid tumors and measurable disease, early or advanced stage.
Planned standard-of-care treatment with a PD-1 or PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitor.
ECOG performance status 0 to 3 and life expectancy of at least 3 months.
Willing to stop or not start daily acetaminophen and THC-containing products during the study.
Willing to take loratadine and aspirin, or continue a similar antihistamine or NSAID already being taken.
not_for: Contraindication to immunotherapy, aspirin, or loratadine, or high bleeding risk from blood thinners or antiplatelet agents.
True allergic reaction to loratadine or aspirin (intolerance does not count).
Immunocompromised, including solid organ transplant, active HIV, or autoimmune disease on immune-modulating drugs.
